hook.line: *Was closed* in English can mean two things: someone closed it, or it was shut when you got there. Spanish makes you pick, and the little verb in front tells the whole story.
hook.es: El café fue cerrado por la alcaldía.
hook.en: The café was closed down by the council.

rule:
English hides this behind one little word: *was closed*. Spanish makes you choose.

*Ser* plus the *-do* word is an event: something happened, and somebody (even if unnamed) did it. It is a moment on a timeline.
*El café fue cerrado.* Someone closed it.

*Estar* plus the *-do* word is a state: the result, as you find it.
*El café estaba cerrado.* It was shut when you got there.

Quick test: did it happen at a moment, done by someone? *Ser*. Is it how you found things? *Estar*.

The ending agrees either way: *cerrado, cerrada, cerrados, cerradas*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the contrast between the passive voice (*ser* plus participle) and the resultant state (*estar* plus participle).

options: The café was shut when I got there.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *fue* or *estaba*: The door was open when I arrived. La puerta ___ abierta.
yourTurn.why: It is how the door was when you got there: *estaba*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *fue* or *estaba*: Someone opened the door, and it was Vale. La puerta ___ abierta por Vale.
yourTurn.answer: La puerta fue abierta por Vale.
yourTurn.why: Someone did it, and you name them with *por*: *fue*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The café was closed. (it was shut when I got there)
Say: The café was closed down by the council.
yourTurn.answer: El café fue cerrado por la alcaldía.
yourTurn.why: An action, with a doer: *fue cerrado por*.
The result, so *están* and a plural ending.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The letter was signed yesterday.
yourTurn.why: *Ayer* marks an event on the timeline, so *fue*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a state: La carta fue firmada.
yourTurn.why: Swap *fue* for *está* and you describe the result.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it an event with a doer: Los platos están lavados. (by Vale)
yourTurn.answer: Los platos fueron lavados por Vale.

pitfalls.wrong: El café fue cerrado cuando llegué.
pitfalls.right: El café estaba cerrado cuando llegué.
pitfalls.why: Almost. You are describing how things were when you arrived, so *estaba*.

pitfalls.wrong: La puerta estaba abierta por Vale.
pitfalls.right: La puerta fue abierta por Vale.
pitfalls.why: When you name who did it with *por*, you are telling an event, so *fue*.
The ending still agrees with what it describes, with *ser* or *estar*.
For the result as it is now, use *está*.

personal: Look at your kitchen. Say one thing that is done with *está* or *están* (for example *Los platos están lavados*), then one thing that someone did with *fue* or *fueron*.
